questoes.enunciado: A 28-year-old patient, after eating shrimp, presents within 10 minutes with generalized urticaria, lip edema, dyspnea with wheezing and hypotension (BP 80/50 mmHg). What is the predominant immunological mechanism, and what is the first-line treatment?
questoes.resposta:
Step-by-step solution:
Identify the clinical picture: onset within minutes of exposure to an allergen (shrimp), with skin (urticaria, angioedema), respiratory (wheezing, dyspnea) and cardiovascular (hypotension) involvement → meets the criteria for anaphylaxis [4,15].
Mechanism: type I hypersensitivity (immediate, IgE-mediated). IgE bound to FcεRI on mast cells. On re-exposure, the allergen cross-links the IgE molecules, causing massive degranulation [6,7,10].
Consequence: vasodilation (hypotension), ↑ permeability (edema, urticaria), bronchoconstriction (wheezing) [6].
First-line treatment: INTRAMUSCULAR ADRENALINE (epinephrine), in the anterolateral thigh [4].
Complementary measures: oxygen, fluid resuscitation, Trendelenburg position; antihistamines and corticosteroids are adjuncts [4].

Answer: Type I hypersensitivity (IgE-mediated) → anaphylaxis. Treatment: IM adrenaline.

questoes.enunciado: A patient presents with anemia (Hb 7.2 g/dL), elevated indirect bilirubin and a positive direct Coombs test. What type of hypersensitivity is this, and what are the three mechanisms of cell destruction involved?
questoes.resposta:
Step-by-step solution:
Interpret: anemia + ↑ indirect bilirubin (hemolysis) + positive direct Coombs (antibodies bound to the erythrocyte surface) → autoimmune hemolytic anemia [6].
Classification: type II hypersensitivity (cytotoxic/cytolytic) — antibodies (IgG/IgM) bind to antigens on the cell surface [6].
Mechanism 1 — Complement activation: classical pathway → membrane attack complex (MAC) → cell lysis [6].
Mechanism 2 — ADCC: cells with Fc receptors (NK cells, macrophages) recognize the antibody Fc and destroy the target cell [6].
Mechanism 3 — Opsonization/phagocytosis: antibodies and C3b coat the cell, facilitating phagocytosis by macrophages [6].

Answer: Type II (cytotoxic). Mechanisms: (1) complement/MAC, (2) ADCC, (3) opsonization/phagocytosis.

questoes.enunciado: A construction worker develops, 48 hours after wearing rubber gloves, an erythematous, vesicular, pruritic eczema on the hands. A contact (patch) test is positive for thiurams. What type of hypersensitivity is this, and what are the predominant cell and cytokine?
questoes.resposta:
Step-by-step solution:
Analyze the timing: onset at 48 hours → delayed reaction [6,13].
A positive patch test confirms allergic contact dermatitis [13].
Classification: type IV hypersensitivity (delayed, cell-mediated) — no antibodies involved [6,7,13].
Predominant cell: CD4+ Th1 lymphocyte previously sensitized to the antigen (rubber hapten) [6,13].
Predominant cytokine: IFN-γ (interferon-gamma), which recruits and activates macrophages [6,13].

Answer: Type IV (delayed, cell-mediated). Cell: Th1 (CD4+). Cytokine: IFN-γ.

questoes.enunciado: The Coombs and Gell classification divides hypersensitivity reactions into four types based mainly on:

alternativas.texto: The clinical severity of the reaction.
The type of immunity (humoral/cellular), the effector and the time of onset.

questoes.comentario: The Coombs and Gell classification (1963) is based on the type of immunity (humoral in types I–III, cellular in IV), the predominant effector and the time to reaction [6,7].

questoes.enunciado: In the sensitization phase of type I hypersensitivity, which cytokine is responsible for class switching of B lymphocytes to IgE production?
questoes.comentario: IL-4 (and IL-13) produced by Th2 lymphocytes promotes class switching of B lymphocytes to IgE production [6,11]. IFN-γ, on the contrary, inhibits IgE production.

questoes.enunciado: The high-affinity receptor for IgE found on the surface of mast cells is called:
questoes.comentario: FcεRI is the high-affinity receptor for the Fc portion of IgE, found on mast cells and basophils. Cross-linking of FcεRI-bound IgE by the allergen triggers degranulation [7,10].

questoes.enunciado: Which of the following mediators is preformed and stored in mast cell granules?
questoes.comentario: Histamine is a preformed mediator, stored in the granules. Leukotrienes, prostaglandins, PAF and cytokines are synthesized de novo during the reaction [6,10].

questoes.enunciado: Type III hypersensitivity is characterized by:

alternativas.texto: Cell destruction by antibodies bound to the surface.
Formation and deposition of immune complexes activating complement.
A reaction mediated by IgE and mast cells.
A delayed reaction mediated by T cells.
Direct activation of neutrophils by haptens.

questoes.comentario: In type III, antigen–antibody complexes (immune complexes) form in antigen excess, deposit in tissues, activate complement and recruit neutrophils, which cause tissue damage [6].

questoes.enunciado: The tuberculin test (PPD), read at 48–72 hours, is an example of which type of hypersensitivity?
questoes.comentario: PPD is a type IV (delayed, cell-mediated) hypersensitivity reaction, mediated by Th1 lymphocytes and IFN-γ. Reading at 48–72 h reflects the time needed for cell recruitment [6].

questoes.enunciado: 'Type 2 inflammation' is characterized mainly by the production of which cytokines?
questoes.comentario: Type 2 inflammation is mediated by Th2 and ILC2 cells, with production of IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13. It is the common substrate of allergic diseases (asthma, rhinitis, atopic dermatitis) [11].

questoes.enunciado: Regarding the late response of type I hypersensitivity, it is correct to state that:

alternativas.texto: It is mediated only by histamine.
It occurs 2–24 hours after exposure, mediated by cytokines and eosinophils.
It does not occur in allergic diseases.
It is equivalent to type IV.

questoes.comentario: The late response (2–24 h) is mediated by cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13) and eosinophil recruitment, characterizing the chronic inflammation of allergic diseases [6,7].

questoes.enunciado: In type II hypersensitivity, which immunoglobulin classes are predominantly involved?
questoes.comentario: Type II hypersensitivity is mediated by IgG and IgM, which bind to antigens on the cell surface and activate complement, ADCC and opsonization [6].

questoes.enunciado: Which Th2-produced cytokine specifically stimulates the production and activation of eosinophils?
questoes.comentario: IL-5 is the key cytokine for the production, maturation, activation and recruitment of eosinophils. For this reason, anti-IL-5 antibodies (mepolizumab) are used in eosinophilic asthma [6,12].

questoes.enunciado: Explain why cross-linking of at least two IgE molecules on the mast cell surface is necessary to trigger degranulation, and what the molecular consequence of this event is.
questoes.resposta: Simple binding of an allergen to a single IgE molecule does not trigger degranulation. The signal is generated when a multivalent allergen (with multiple epitopes) cross-links two or more IgE molecules already bound to adjacent FcεRI. This cross-linking brings the receptors together, causing phosphorylation of the ITAMs (immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motifs) in the intracellular portion of FcεRI by Src-family kinases (such as Lyn). The downstream cascade (involving Syk, LAT, PLCγ) leads to an increase in intracellular calcium and PKC activation, resulting in fusion of the granules with the membrane (exocytosis) and release of the preformed mediators, in addition to activation of the phospholipase pathway for synthesis of lipid mediators [6,7,10]. Without cross-linking there is no receptor aggregation and therefore no signal — hence the need for allergen multivalency.

questoes.enunciado: Discuss the concept of 'type 2 inflammation' and justify, on mechanistic grounds, the use of biologics such as dupilumab, mepolizumab and omalizumab in severe allergic diseases.
questoes.resposta:
Type 2 inflammation is the common immunological substrate of allergic diseases (asthma, rhinitis, atopic dermatitis), mediated by Th2 and ILC2, with production of IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13 [11]. Each biologic acts at a specific point:
• Omalizumab (anti-IgE): binds circulating IgE, preventing its binding to FcεRI → reduces sensitization of mast cells/basophils [12].
• Mepolizumab (anti-IL-5): blocks IL-5, reducing eosinophils → useful in the eosinophilic phenotype of asthma [12].
• Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα): blocks the shared receptor of IL-4 and IL-13, acting on the central pathway → inhibits IgE production and eosinophil recruitment [11,12].
The logic is mechanistic and stratified: identifying the phenotype makes it possible to choose the therapeutic target. GINA has incorporated this concept [8].

questoes.enunciado: An Rh-negative (Rh-) pregnant woman has an Rh+ fetus. Explain the immunological mechanism of hemolytic disease of the newborn (HDN), the type of hypersensitivity involved and the prevention strategy.
questoes.resposta: HDN is a type II hypersensitivity (cytotoxic) [6]. The mechanism: during pregnancy or delivery, Rh+ fetal red blood cells enter the Rh- maternal circulation. The maternal immune system recognizes the D (Rh) antigen as foreign and produces anti-D IgG. In a subsequent pregnancy with an Rh+ fetus, maternal anti-D IgG crosses the placenta (IgG crosses the placental barrier; IgM does not), binds to fetal erythrocytes and causes hemolysis by complement and opsonization/phagocytosis → fetal anemia, jaundice, hydrops. Prevention consists of administering anti-D immunoglobulin (RhIG) to the Rh- mother in at-risk situations and as prenatal prophylaxis (28th week). RhIG neutralizes the fetal red cells before the mother mounts an active immune response [6]. This is passive tolerogenesis.

questoes.enunciado: Differentiate, from the immunological and temporal standpoint, the 'immediate response' from the 'late response' in type I hypersensitivity, and relate each one to the pathophysiology of asthma.
questoes.resposta:
Immediate (early) response: occurs 5–30 minutes after allergen exposure, mediated mainly by histamine and leukotrienes released in mast cell degranulation. Clinically, it corresponds to acute bronchospasm (wheezing, sudden-onset dyspnea). It is rapid and reversible with bronchodilators [6].
Late response: occurs 2–24 hours after exposure, mediated by cytokines (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, TNF-α) synthesized de novo and by eosinophil recruitment [6,7]. In asthma, it corresponds to the chronic inflammation of the airways — edema, mucus hypersecretion, eosinophilic infiltrate and, in the long term, remodeling. The late response underpins the use of inhaled corticosteroids (which inhibit cytokine transcription) in maintenance treatment [8]. This distinction explains why an asthmatic may worsen hours after exposure, even after initial relief.

questoes.enunciado: In the PHC setting, a patient with a history of wasp-sting anaphylaxis is referred for guidance. What are the WAO (2020) recommendations for post-event management and prevention of recurrence, and why is the use of adrenaline considered suboptimal worldwide? Relate this to the competencies of the 2025 Medicine DCN (CNE/CES Res. No. 3/2025) [5].
questoes.resposta:
The WAO Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020 establishes that, after an episode of anaphylaxis, the patient should be referred to a specialist (allergology) to: (1) identify the cause (history, skin tests, specific IgE, possibly BAT); (2) education of the patient and family; (3) prescription of and training in the use of an adrenaline auto-injector; (4) a written, individualized action plan; (5) guidance on avoidance of the trigger; (6) consideration of specific immunotherapy (for hymenopteran venom, highly effective) [4].
The WAO emphasizes that adrenaline use remains suboptimal worldwide, owing to: delayed recognition, underuse, lack of availability and cost of auto-injectors, and inadequate prescribing. In Brazilian PHC, even where the auto-injector is hard to obtain, the physician must educate, train and ensure referral [4].
Relation to the 2025 DCN [5]: it integrates competencies of CNE/CES Res. No. 3/2025: evidence-based clinical reasoning (item III); comprehensive care with PHC as coordinator (item VI); evidence-based medicine (item X); action in emergencies (item XIV); health education (items II and XIX); and equity of access (items XI and XXV).
